chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a man who trimmed one nail from his nails while he was in the state of ihram.
He عليه السلام said: "He must give a mudd of food until they reach ten. If he trims all the fingers of his hands, then a sheep's blood-sacrifice is due upon him."

I said: "What if he trims all the nails of his hands and feet?" So he عليه السلام said: "If he did that in one sitting, then one blood-sacrifice is due upon him; and if he did it separately in two sittings, then two blood-sacrifices are due upon him."

key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: the sacrifice of a sheep as expiation
key_terms.ظُفُرًا: a single nail that has been trimmed
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a prescribed measure of food given as expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah for trimming nails while in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on trimming nails while in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah. It specifies graduated expiation: a mudd of food for each nail up to ten, a sheep if all fingernails are trimmed, and one or two sacrifices depending on whether the fingernails and toenails were trimmed in one sitting or two.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2689 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man in the state of ihram who trimmed one of his nails.
Imam (as) said: "He must give a mudd of food as expiation. If he trims ten nails, he must sacrifice a sheep."

I asked: "What if he trims the nails of both his hands and feet?"
Imam (as) said: "If he does this in one sitting, he must offer one sacrifice. If he does it in two separate sittings, he must offer two sacrifices."
